messages:
maria: FYI customers hitting duplicate SSE messages when a stream hits a proxy 204 with no body and client auto-reconnects. seen in canary and a prod tenant.
oliver: 204? we treat 204 as terminal close right now. why are clients reconnecting?
maria: some mobile SDKs interpret a keepalive-less 204 as transient and reopen. backend sets `X-Last-Event: E42` so backend thinks it terminated gracefully but client thinks it dropped.
nina: logs: 
```
[proxy] GET /stream resume_token=rt-9 -> 204 Content-Length:0 X-Last-Event:E42
[client] websocket: disconnected, reconnecting (no heartbeat)
[backend] on_connect resume_token=rt-9 -> replay from E40..E42
```
kevin: ah that replay is exactly the dup window. router returns 204 without `X-Resume-Ok` header so clients unsure. we currently only set `X-Stream-Ended: true` which is ambiguous.
ops-bot: alert: streaming_duplicate_rate tenant=t-prod-88 +0.9% at 2026-03-20T20:11Z
oliver: routing policy debate: change proxy to include `X-Resume-Intent: none|available` or treat 204 as "sticky-close" vs "soft-close". which is better?
nina: short-term hack: treat 204 with X-Last-Event as a soft-close -> don't let router trigger immediate replay unless client sent explicit resume. that prevents backend from re-sending on reconnect.
kevin: longer-term: introduce resume-disambiguation header from backend: `X-Resume-Validation: token=rt-9;last=E42;sig=abc`. Router can validate signature against lease service before forwarding. Expensive but exact.
oliver: cost tradeoff: validate synchronously on router adds ~20ms median and p99 variable. Could gate behind feature flag for tenants with sensitive billing.
console-team: telemetry gap: our stream metrics lump all 204 into `stream_close` and we lose resume vs final close. propose new tags: close_type=(final|soft|protocol), resume_token_present=(true|false), resume_validation_ms.
maria: also need a quick alert: if duplicate_rate > 0.5% for 15m -> page. AND a dashboard showing last-event lag histogram.
kevin: rollout idea: phase 1: change proxy to emit `X-Close-Type: soft|final` when backend sets last-event but no explicit final flag. phase 2: router honors `X-Close-Type` and suppresses automatic replay for soft. phase 3: enable resume-validation header check for 10% canary of enterprise tenants.
oliver: implementation notes: config: 
```
stream_close_policy:
  treat_204_as: soft_if_last_event
  resume_validation:
    enabled: false
    timeout_ms: 40
    sig_key: env(RESUME_SIG_KEY)
```
nina: server-side de-dupe helpful too: keep last_seen_event per session for 90s and drop duplicates. low overhead and buys time for rollout.
ops-bot: infra note: adding sync resume validation will increase router CPU and histogram latency tagging. put `resume_validation_ms` into trace span.
deploy-bot: planned deploy: 2026-03-22T03:00Z - canary 5% us-east with `treat_204_as_soft` enabled.
console-team: we'll add `close_type` breakdown and resume_validation_ms histogram to the streaming ops dashboard and add a sampling trace for 1% resumes.
maria: runbook please: steps to detect and mitigate: 1) query metrics `streaming_duplicate_rate` by tenant 2) check logs for 204 + X-Last-Event 3) enable server-side dedupe 4) roll flag back. can someone draft?
oliver: I'll draft the runbook and open PR for proxy header change. assigning to me + nina for router change.
maria: thanks. I'll follow up with affected customers and open support tickets for potential billing adjustments.
_meta: generated_by: synthetic-thread-gen; topic: streaming SSE 204 semantics, resume headers, routing policy, telemetry and rollout
